Class UsbHostShield

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.usb.UsbHostShield
public final class UsbHostShield extends Object
The Arduino USB Host Shield: a Maxim MAX3421E USB host controller driven over Spi as plain Java, so it needs no Arduino library. It hosts one full- or low-speed device plugged straight into the shield's USB-A socket (no hubs), gives it address 1, and offers the control, bulk IN and bulk OUT transfers a device driver such as Cp210xSerial builds on. 
UsbHostShield usb = new UsbHostShield();   // once, at startup
if (usb.begin() && usb.attach()) {
    // usb.vendorId(), usb.productId(), usb.controlIn(...), usb.bulkIn(...)
}

The shield reaches the controller through the ICSP header's SPI pins and selects it with D10; its interrupt line on D9 is not used (the driver polls), so D9 stays free, but D10 to D13 do not. The device's 5 V comes from the board: a device that draws a lot (a spinning lidar, a hard disk) may need the board powered from an external supply.

Allocation: the constructor allocates the 8-byte setup packet and two 16-entry toggle tables; every transfer is allocation-free and writes into caller-owned buffers. Transfers return a byte count, or a negative ERROR_* code; they never throw.

See Also:
  • MAX3421E programming guide

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public boolean begin()
      Starts the bus, resets the controller and puts it in host mode. Returns false when the controller does not come back from its reset or does not identify itself: the shield is missing or not seated on the ICSP header.

    • revision

      public int revision()
      The controller's silicon revision: 0x12 or 0x13 on a working shield, anything else when not.

    • isDeviceConnected

      public boolean isDeviceConnected()
      Samples the bus and reports whether a device holds one of its data lines up, connected or not enumerated.

    • attach

      public boolean attach()
      Waits for the bus to settle, resets it, and enumerates the connected device: reads its device descriptor, gives it DEVICE_ADDRESS, and reads the descriptor again for vendorId() and productId(). Returns false when no device is connected or it does not answer. Takes about a quarter of a second.

    • isAttached

      public boolean isAttached()
      Whether attach() enumerated a device.

    • isLowSpeed

      public boolean isLowSpeed()
      Whether the attached device is a low-speed (1.5 Mbit/s) one rather than full speed (12 Mbit/s).

    • vendorId

      public int vendorId()
      The attached device's USB vendor ID, from its device descriptor.

    • productId

      public int productId()
      The attached device's USB product ID, from its device descriptor.

    • maxPacketSize0

      public int maxPacketSize0()
      The largest packet the attached device's control endpoint takes, from its device descriptor.

    • configurationDescriptor

      public int configurationDescriptor(byte[] buffer, int length)
      Reads the device's configuration descriptor, with its interfaces and endpoints, into buffer: up to length bytes. Returns the bytes read, or a negative ERROR_* code.

    • setConfiguration

      public int setConfiguration(int value)
      Selects configuration value and restarts every endpoint's data toggle. Returns 0 or an error code.

    • controlIn

      public int controlIn(int requestType, int request, int value, int index, byte[] buffer, int length)
      A control transfer that reads up to length bytes from the device into buffer: setup, data IN and status stages. Returns the bytes read, or a negative ERROR_* code.

    • controlOut

      public int controlOut(int requestType, int request, int value, int index, byte[] data, int length)
      A control transfer that sends the first length bytes of data to the device (none when length is 0): setup, data OUT and status stages. Returns 0, or a negative ERROR_* code.

    • bulkIn

      public int bulkIn(int endpoint, byte[] buffer, int offset, int maxPacketSize)
      Asks bulk IN endpoint (its number, 1 to 15, without the direction bit) for one packet and stores it at buffer[offset]. Does not wait: returns 0 when the device has nothing to send (it answered NAK), the bytes received, or a negative ERROR_* code. buffer needs room for maxPacketSize bytes from offset; a longer packet is cut.

    • bulkOut

      public int bulkOut(int endpoint, byte[] data, int offset, int length, int maxPacketSize)
      Sends length bytes from data[offset] to bulk OUT endpoint, in packets of up to maxPacketSize bytes. Returns the bytes sent, or a negative ERROR_* code.
